correctness.rationale: The inspected Black–De Loera primary text gives Q vertices exactly the signed permutations (2,1,…,1), and Q facets exactly <s,x>≤k+1 for sign s∈{−1,0,1}^d, k=|supp s|≥1. Thus every Q vertex has squared norm d+3, yielding Q minimum covering radius √(d+3), and every facet has origin-distance (k+1)/√k with binom(d,k)2^k faces and minimum2. By polarity, each Σ facet corresponding to a Q vertex has origin-distance 1/√(d+3), all d2^d touch the same ball; each Σ vertex is s/(k+1), norm √k/(k+1) and max1/2 at support1. Differences of squared shell radii show strict increase/decrease. Opposite supporting facets and antipodal extreme vertices show the origin is the unique relevant Euclidean extremal center in both bodies. Every dimension d≥2 follows symbolically; inspected verify.py enumerates d=2..7 and LP facets only corroboratively.

These formulas are short once the parent vertex/facet structures are known but organize nontrivial uniform geometric information of a natural object, rather than an arbitrary isolated small numerical case.

final_claim: For canonical Σ_d=(C_d+◇_d)^∘ and Q_d=C_d+◇_d, all Σ facets are tangent to one sphere r=1/√(d+3); Q has circumradius √(d+3), inradius2, and d strict facet-distance shells (k+1)/√k; Σ has circumradius1/2 and d strict vertex shells √k/(k+1), with multiplicities binom(d,k)2^k and unique Euclidean centers, for every d≥2.
limitations: Applies to the standard Euclidean canonical polar Σ_d, not arbitrary affine signohedron realizations.
